title: Culture and Negotiation
description: Cultural expectations shape whether people prefer direct confrontation, use silence, prioritize relationships, or need face-saving.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Cultural expectations shape whether people prefer direct confrontation, use silence, prioritize relationships, or need face-saving.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: A Northern European counterpart says 'That won't work' flatly. It's not rudeness; it's directness.
An East Asian counterpart goes silent after a proposal. It may mean 'I need to think,' not rejection.
In the Middle East or Latin America, negotiating entirely by email without a relationship-building meeting first can kill the deal.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
content: Pushing for a 'yes' when they are using 'yes' to mean 'I hear you,' not agreement.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Before negotiating with someone from a different culture, ask a local contact: 'What's the biggest mistake outsiders make when negotiating here?' That one question saves more deals than any textbook.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: When in doubt, slow down, ask more questions, and observe. Cultural missteps often come from speed, not intent.
